title.rendered: Very Low-Earth Orbit: How the Space Force Is Exploring Ops at Lower Altitudes

excerpt.rendered: As commercial companies, universities, and research agencies develop new approaches to operating satellites at lower and lower altitudes, the Space Force is taking notice and considering how it might leverage those advances in both the near and long term.

title.rendered: Pentagon Loans $150M to LeoLabs to Build Ground Radars

excerpt.rendered: The Pentagon’s Office of Strategic Capital announced a $150 million loan agreement to space intelligence company LeoLabs to expand its manufacturing capacity and add dozens of radars to its global network by 2030.

title.rendered: Space Force Chief Eyes Growth in Components to Meet Operational Demand

excerpt.rendered: The Space Force wants to increase the size of its components to better support combatant commands in the coming years, according to Chief of Space Operations Gen. Douglas Schiess. “We’re going to add 2,800 Guardians and 2,000 civilians in fiscal 2027 if the budget comes through,” Schiess said Nov. 4 at an event hosted by AFA’s Mitchell Institute for Aerospace Studies. “A lot of that will go into our components.”
